title: SMAT 2026: Jitesh, Samad star in thrilling chases
excerpt: Elsewhere, debutant Jamshed Alam had a spectacular start to his T20 career, snaring four wickets in four balls for Railways against Saurashtra
author: Cricbuzz Staff
body: Openers Atharva Taide and Danish Malewar laid the base for Vidarbha’s chase in a rain-hit 13-overs-a-side game against Gujarat. Despite a late hiccup, Vidarbha chased down 129 off the penultimate ball. Earlier, Gujarat suffered a collapse of their own, after openers Aarya Desai (41 off 23) and Urvil Patel (35 off 16) raced to a quick start. Parth Rekhade’s three-fer kept them under 130.

Himachal captain Pukhraj Mann struck 61 off 31, trumping his opposite number Manisankar Murasingh’s four-fer to carry them to 183 against Tripura. Then Rohit Kumar and Aryaman Dhaliwal took three each, first reducing them to 37/3, and eventually leaving them 32 runs short, despite a fighting fifty from No.5 Lakshay Thareja.

Keeper Kunal Singh Rathore’s unbeaten century was the highlight of Rajasthan’s 67-run win over Mizoram. Helped by cameos from the middle-order trio of Kartik Sharma, Mukul Choudhary and Mahipal Lomror, they racked up 224/5. Chinmay Sutar continued his fine batting run with a 25-ball 48, but Mizoram fell comfortably short.

Debutant Jamshed Alam had a spectacular start to his T20 career, snaring four wickets in four balls for Railways against Saurashtra. As many as five Saurashtra players fell for ducks, and Alam finished with 5 for 38. Chasing 183, a lone effort by Harvansh Pangalia (80) couldn’t stand against Alam’s dream debut, even as Krains Fuletra at No.10 smashed 36 off 23 alongside U19 hero Mohit Ulva (22 off 15) to reduce the defeat margin.

Mumbai cruised to a nine-wicket win over Chattisgarh, with Angkrish Raghuvanshi bouncing back from a duck to score 84* in a chase of 160. Hardik Tamore (41) and Musheer Khan (29) added useful support acts. Earlier, Shivam Dube was the pick of the bowlers, taking 3 for 21. Chattisgarh’s 17-year-old sensation Vikalp Tiwari struck 41 off 18 – eight fours included – but didn’t get much support from the rest of the top order.

Sanju Samson fell for 17 off 9, but fifties from keeper-opener Mohammed Azharuddin and Rohan Kunnummal, and a brisk cameo by Vishnu Vinod propelled Kerala to 204/4. MD Nidheesh then cut through Puducherry’s top order. Despite Prasad Pawar’s 67, and brisk knocks from Ankit Sharma (45) and Sagar Trivedi (34), Kerala were left 18 short.

The in-form Priyansh Arya fired again as part of a dominating performance by Delhi’s top-order, with contributions from Yash Dhull and Nitish Rana powering them to 232/6. But the headliner was Tejasvi Dahiya at No.4, smashing 95 off 36. In response, Haryana couldn’t match the scoring rate, with Suyash Sharma finishing with a three-fer, and Mayank Yadav taking two.

Veteran left-arm seamer Chama Milind took four as Uttarakhand were bowled out for 146 against Hyderabad. His new-ball partner Chinntla Readdi took three, as a top-order collapse first, and another towards the end saw them lose their last six for 22 runs. Hyderabad’s pursuit was held together by Kodimela Himateja’s 77, and despite wickets falling around him, it was enough to wrap up the chase in the 16th over.

Jitesh Sharma’s 54 off 29 outshone Abhimanyu Easwaran’s 78 off 46, starring in Baroda’s chase of 173 against Bengal. Skipper Krunal Pandya and Safvan Patel claimed identical figures of 2-33, hitting Bengal in different phases of their innings. Baroda’s reply was anchored by Shashwat Rawat’s 51 off 35, before Jitesh’s blitz took them through.

Madhya Pradesh eked out a five-run win over Maharashtra, surviving a late Arshin Kulkarni fifty that nearly took the game from them. Two run outs of the last two balls ended Maharashtra’s chase, which began with fifties from openers Prithvi Shaw and Sahil Parakh. Kumar Kartikeya’s 2 for 33 slowed them down in the middle before Kulkarni hauled them up. MP’s openers Harsh Gawali and Akshat Raghuwanshi, too, hit fifties, while Rajat Patidar struck 31 off 18, helping them to 208/9.

Karnataka were shot out for 95 against Chandigarh, with Hardik Chowdhry and Bhagmender Lather taking three each to never really allow them to let going. Karun Nair was the top-scorer with 25 off 22. In reply, captain Shivam Bhambri struck a fifty to polish off the chase in 14 overs.

Jammu & Kashmir pulled off a stunning chase against Punjab, with Abdul Samad’s 64* off 27 taking them through. No.7 Lone Muzaffar hit a six off the penultimate ball, lending support to Samad who hit seven sixes in his blitz. Opener Qamran Iqbal set the base with a fifty, before Harpreet Brar’s spell slowed them down. Punjab’s total of 195 was anchored by Vivaan Malhotra’s 85 off 59, while Ramandeep Singh brought up a fifty in the backend.
Note: All three Plate matches (Arunachal Pradesh vs Nagaland, Sikkim vs Meghalaya and Services vs Meghalaya) in Sovima, Nagaland were abandoned due to rain.
